title: Weekly restore drill into den, a failover runbook, and loopctl watched from outside

story.as_a: factory that depends on one database and one public URL
story.i_want_to: prove every week that loopctl's database restores in the failover region, and record from outside loopctl whenever a region stops answering
story.so_that: a lost database or a dark region becomes a timed, rehearsed procedure and a work item, never a surprise found by Mark

rationale: PRD R9: the database stays single-primary with tested backups and a written failover runbook, and loopctl is monitored from outside loopctl. loopctl's database lives on ecf-postgres in lax, backed up nightly by pgBackRest to Tigris (infra postgres/ecf-backup.sh), but infra's restore runbook marks the total-loss restore NEVER REHEARSED and the PITR drill unscheduled (infra runbooks/postgres-restore.md:15-16,771). A den machine (US-52.60) helps only while the lax database answers, so the failover that matters is restoring the database somewhere else, and only a scheduled drill keeps that capability real. Nothing outside loopctl watches it today: infra's external probe covers home-care-billing only (infra scripts/jobs/hcb-availability.sh).

acceptance_criteria.description: deploy/restore-drill.sh creates a scratch Fly app loopctl-restore-drill-<run id> with one machine and one new volume in den from the ecf-postgres image, restores the newest pgBackRest backup of stanza ecf with WAL to the latest point into it, and starts Postgres there.

The drill passes only when, on the restored loopctl database, the newest schema_migrations version equals production's, every index named in deploy/restore-drill-checks.sql is valid, and max(story_stage_events.inserted_at) is no older than 36 h before the drill started.
The drill destroys its scratch app, machine and volume on every exit path, success, failure or interrupt, and refuses to start while another loopctl-restore-drill-* app exists.
The drill prints one JSON line {result, restore_seconds, data_age_seconds, backup_label, region} and writes it as the workflow's artifact, so each run records the measured restore time and data age.
.github/workflows/restore-drill.yml runs the drill weekly on [self-hosted, fleet-ci] in concurrency group restore-drill, with a Tigris key that can read the backup bucket and cannot delete from it.

.github/workflows/uptime.yml runs every 5 minutes on [self-hosted, fleet-ci] in concurrency group uptime and probes https://loopctl.com/health once per region in deploy/regions.txt with header fly-prefer-region; a region is down when two probes 30 s apart both fail to return 200 with that region in the body.

A failed drill or a down region opens one issue on mkreyman/loopctl labelled restore-drill or loopctl-outage, or comments on the one already open with that label; the next passing run closes it with the window it covered, so each failure is one issue and becomes a work item through the repo's intake.

test_cases.name: the drill's flyctl sequence, cleanup on failure and the second-run guard (unit, stub flyctl)
preconditions: a temp dir first on PATH with a stub flyctl that logs argv and fails the restore step; a stub listing no drill app, then one
steps: run it with the stub listing an existing loopctl-restore-drill-x app
expected_results: the log shows apps create, volumes create --region den, machine run --region den, then apps destroy after the failure; exit 1. The second run exits 1 naming the existing app and logs no create

test_cases.name: an interrupt still destroys the scratch app (unit, stub flyctl)
preconditions: a stub flyctl whose restore step sleeps
steps: start the drill with Port.open, send SIGTERM during the restore step
expected_results: the log ends with apps destroy loopctl-restore-drill-<run id> --yes

test_cases.name: the verification SQL passes on a migrated test database and fails on a stale one (DataCase, async: false: reads schema_migrations of the shared test database)
preconditions: the test database migrated; one story_stage_events row inserted now
steps: run deploy/restore-drill-checks.sql with the production version set to the latest migration
run it with the production version set to a version not present
run it with the drill start set 37 h after the newest event
expected_results: pass; fail naming schema_migrations; fail naming data age

test_cases.name: the result line shape (unit, stub flyctl and psql)
steps: run the drill and parse its last stdout line
expected_results: JSON with result pass, integer restore_seconds and data_age_seconds, a backup_label and region den

test_cases.name: both workflows run on fleet-ci, serialized, on their schedules (unit, YamlElixir)
steps: read on.schedule, runs-on, concurrency and the env names of each
expected_results: restore-drill weekly, uptime */5; both [self-hosted, fleet-ci]; groups restore-drill and uptime with cancel-in-progress false; the drill's Tigris secret is the read-only one

test_cases.name: the probe tells a region down from a region answered by another, and files one issue (unit, stub curl and gh)
preconditions: deploy/uptime-probe.sh with stubs: curl answering den requests with body region lax; gh issue list answering an open loopctl-outage issue on the second run
steps: run it with curl answering den correctly
expected_results: first run: one gh issue create labelled loopctl-outage naming den; second run: one gh issue comment and no create; third run: gh issue close with the window

test_cases.name: a failed drill files or comments on the restore-drill issue (unit, stub gh)
preconditions: the drill's result line with result fail; gh stubs with and without an open restore-drill issue
steps: run the workflow's report step script deploy/report-ops-result.sh against each stub
expected_results: create when none is open, comment when one is; a pass result closes an open one

technical_notes: Backups today: nightly pgBackRest full at 08:17 UTC on ecf-postgres, stanza ecf, Tigris bucket ecf-postgres-backups path /ecf, 14 days time-based retention, WAL archived continuously (infra runbooks/postgres-restore.md:69-80; infra postgres/ecf-backup.sh:1-20). The backup set is the whole cluster, so the drill restores every database into the scratch volume and checks loopctl's only; the scratch app is destroyed with it, and listen_addresses='localhost' plus archive_mode=off keep it unreachable and from writing WAL to the live repository (infra runbooks/postgres-restore.md:177-185).

Image: the ecf-postgres image from infra postgres/build-and-push.sh (REF registry.fly.io/<app>:pgvector-<hash>, :39-40); the drill takes the image ref of the running ecf-postgres machine from `flyctl machines list -a ecf-postgres --json`, so it restores with the same Postgres and pgvector versions.

Credentials: a Tigris access key scoped read-only to ecf-postgres-backups, stored as the repo secret BACKUP_READ_TIGRIS_KEY/BACKUP_READ_TIGRIS_SECRET and passed to the scratch machine only, never written to the live machine. Mirrors the separate-blast-radius rule of infra scripts/jobs/postgres-archive.sh:10-23. FLY_API_TOKEN is the deploy job's.

Check SQL: deploy/restore-drill-checks.sql takes the production schema_migrations max version (read through loopctl's own read path before the restore) and the drill start time as psql variables; the index list is the HNSW indexes on article_embeddings and the stories/story_stage_events primary keys, compared with pg_index.indisvalid. infra runbooks/postgres-restore.md:386-421 lists today's eight HNSW indexes on loopctl.

Runbook: docs/factory/runbooks/failover.md (beside the release-1 runbook docs/factory/runbooks/merge-duplicate-projects.md) states the two failures and their steps: a lax machine lost (nothing to do: den and the second lax machine serve, US-52.60), and the database lost (run the drill's procedure against a non-scratch app in den, point DATABASE_URL and ADMIN_DATABASE_URL at it with fly secrets set, deploy). Its measured RTO and RPO come from the drill's latest artifact; it cites infra runbooks/postgres-restore.md for ecf-postgres's own operations rather than copying them.

Monitor: GET /health (lib/loopctl_web/router.ex:146, unauthenticated, LoopctlWeb.HealthController moduledoc :24-25) with fly-prefer-region; Fly answers from another region when the asked one has no healthy machine, which is why the body's region field (US-52.60) decides. The same outside-the-watched-thing rule as infra decisions/0016 and scripts/jobs/hcb-availability.sh:1-24.

No paging (PRD R4): failures become one labelled issue each, deduplicated by the open-issue-per-label rule under the workflow's concurrency group, and reach the loop through the loopctl repo's intake source like any issue. GitHub schedules are best effort, so a 5-minute cron can run late; the issue's window is from the first failed probe to the first passing one.

deploy/report-ops-result.sh is the one script both workflows call to open, comment on or close the labelled issue, with GITHUB_TOKEN under permissions issues: write. uptime.yml also takes a workflow_dispatch input `regions` that replaces deploy/regions.txt for that run, so the alarm path can be exercised against a region with no machine.
non_goals: A standing replica or automatic database failover: after the first incident (PRD R9).
Moving ecf-postgres's own backup, archive and health jobs out of infra: they serve six databases and stay there.
Who acts on an outage issue: the loop places it like any work item (release 5 visibility; intake from release 6).

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.63.6: the probe runs on the fleet, outside Fly and outside loopctl, so a partition that isolates loopctl is seen by the probe instead of silencing it.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.63.7: each failure's record is one GitHub issue with its window, and each drill's measurement is a workflow artifact; nothing about an outage is held only inside the loopctl it describes.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.63.7: a re-run finds the open issue for its label and comments on it, so a retried or overlapping run never opens a second issue; AC-52.63.3: a second drill refuses while a scratch app exists.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.63.6: a region counts as down only after two probes 30 s apart fail, so one slow answer does not open an issue.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.63.1: the drill restores in den, the failover region, so the same steps the runbook gives for a lost database are the ones exercised every week.

definition_of_done: One workflow_dispatch run of restore-drill.yml passes, its artifact shows region den with restore_seconds and data_age_seconds, and `flyctl apps list` afterwards shows no loopctl-restore-drill-* app.
docs/factory/runbooks/failover.md is merged with the measured RTO and RPO from that run.

A workflow_dispatch run of uptime.yml with a regions input naming ord (a region with no loopctl machine) opens one loopctl-outage issue naming ord, and the next scheduled run, on deploy/regions.txt, closes it with its window.
defaults: Drill cadence: weekly, Sundays 11:13 UTC, clear of the 08:17 UTC nightly backup and its stanza lock (owner may change).
Probe cadence: every 5 minutes; down after two failed probes 30 s apart.
Data-age bound for a passing drill: 36 h, the backup-freshness budget infra already uses.
